I had some simulation code that was done in the Random Fields R library, I am converting code to TMB and doing some validations with simulating spatial random effects with matern covariance. messages.subject: sdrep difficulties between Mac/PC
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
 I have been developing a stock assessment package using TMB and fit the models using Jim Thorson's "fit_tmb" code (https://github.com/kaskr/TMB_contrib_R/tree/master/TMBhelper/R) and have found that when I fit a specific model using my Mac, I can get the standard errors of the derived quantities successfully from the sdrep function. However, when I fit the exact same model/code on my PC, the sdrep function returns pdHess==TRUE, but all the standard errors of the derived quantities are NaN. Has anyone else found differences in model outputs between PC/MAC?
Thanks,
Grant

--
Grant Adams
School of Aquatic Fishery Sciences
University of Washington
https://grantdadams.wordpress.com/

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] New data macros
messages.body_plain:
1. Find source code:

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/tmb__core_8hpp_source.html#l00249

2. Current definition of DATA_MATRIX:

#define DATA_MATRIX(name)                                               \
matrix<Type> name(asMatrix<Type>(                                       \
getListElement(TMB_OBJECTIVE_PTR -> data, #name, &Rf_isMatrix)));

3. Replace 'Type' with 'double':

#define DATA_DMATRIX(name)                                              \
matrix<double> name(asMatrix<double>(                                   \
getListElement(TMB_OBJECTIVE_PTR -> data, #name, &Rf_isMatrix)));

From: tmb-...@googlegroups.com <tmb-...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Alan <crosstr...@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, October 17, 2019 7:55:59 AM
To: TMB Users
Subject: [TMB users] New data macros

Hi can anyone guide me on how I would write a macro that could read data from R and store it as a double.

e.g., DATA_DMATRIX(x);

here x is of type matrix<double> as opposed to matrix<Type>.

Thanks

--

recommend doing the calculations in the log-space as far as possible,

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Zero-truncated poisson lognormal
messages.body_plain:
I agree with Ben that you should look into using a Poisson distribution with observation-level random effect. I've been able to generate data using the poilog package in R (from Engen et al. 2002) which results in comparable likelihoods calculated from dpoilog and TMB using a Poisson with an observation-level random effect. The TMB model can easily be extended to treat the random effects as arriving from a spatial-temporal process.

On Fri, Oct 18, 2019 at 2:38 AM Bert van der Veen <brrtj...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hello all,
>
> I'm attempting to fit the model from Engen et al. 2011 ("Estimating similarity of communities: a parametric approach to spatio-temporal analysis of species diversity"), who employ a zero-truncated poisson lognormal distribution to estimate the similarity between two communities, when the sampling intensity is unknown.
>
> Unfortunately, the optimizer is unable to evaluate the function returned by TMB at the (true) starting values, so I suspect there is an issue with either my code, or the combination of the model and the laplace approximation.
>
> Any feedback, suggestions or improvements are greatly appreciated.
>
> TMB-code
> #include <TMB.hpp>
> #include<math.h>
>
> template<class Type>
> Type objective_function<Type>::operator() ()
> {
>   DATA_MATRIX(y);
>
>   PARAMETER_VECTOR(u);
>   PARAMETER_VECTOR(rho);
>   PARAMETER_VECTOR(lg_sigma);
>   PARAMETER_VECTOR(mu);
>
>   vector <Type> sigma = exp(lg_sigma);
>
>   int n = y.cols();
>   int p = y.rows();
>
>   using namespace density;
>   Type nll = 0.0;
>
>   for (int j=0; j<p;j++){
>         Type q = 1.0;
>         Type q0 = 1.0;
>         for (int i=0; i<n;i++){
>          q *= (exp(u(i)*sigma(i)*y(j,i)+mu(i)*y(j,i)-exp(-(u(i)*sigma(i)+mu(i))))/exp(lfactorial(y(j,i))));
>          q0 *= exp(-exp(-(u(i)*sigma(i)+mu(i))));
>         }
>         q *= exp(-1*UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho)(u));
>         q0 *= exp(-1*UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho)(u));
>
>     nll -= log(q/(1-q0));
>   }
>
>   REPORT(UNSTRUCTURED_CORR(rho).cov());
>
>   return nll;
>
> }
>
> R-code
> library(poilog)
>
> y <- rbipoilog(S=100, mu1=1, mu2=2, sig1=1, sig2=2, rho=0.7, nu1=0.5, nu2=0.7)
> sigma <- c(1, 2)
> mu<-c(1, 2)
> rho <- 0.7
> u <- c(0.5, 0.7)
>
> library(TMB)
> compile(file="TMB.cpp")
>
> dyn.load(dynlib("TMB"))
> objr <- MakeADFun(
>   data = list(y = y),
>   parameters = list(u=u, rho=rho, lg_sigma=log(sigma), mu=mu),
>   DLL = "TMB",
>   random="u")
>
> opt<-optim(objr$par,objr$fn,objr$gr,method="BFGS")
>
> dyn.unload(dynlib("TMB"))
>
> Bert
>

> --
